content:
Apple's fall iPhone lineup this year is reportedly set to revolve around the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. Here are the three most important feature differences—excluding price—that could influence your upgrade decision.

Design: Traditional vs. Foldable

This difference is the most obvious, but it's worth mentioning because it's also the most important.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will retain the basic design that iPhones have used for years. Screen sizes and overall design are reportedly identical to the previous generation. If you prefer the feel of a traditional iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top choice.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will be Apple's first foldable model. It features a completely different design, with an outer screen that is shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, and an inner screen similar to an iPad mini.

Camera: Pro Still Leads the Way

Apple has consistently reserved its most cutting-edge and innovative camera technology for the Pro models. This year is no exception.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to feature mostly the same camera capabilities as the iPhone 18 Pro, with one major exception: it will not have a telephoto lens.

According to reports, the iPhone Ultra will still sport the same main lens, ultra-wide lens, and front-facing camera as the Pro series. However, the telephoto lens will remain exclusive to the Pro, and is expected to see further improvements this year.

Performance: Both Run on the A20 Pro Chip, but Materials Affect Performance

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are expected to feature the A20 Pro chip. However, actual performance may vary due to differences in design and materials.

The iPhone 18 Pro will adopt the same all-aluminum unibody design as the iPhone 17 Pro, and will also include a vapor chamber for cooling. These two changes boosted the iPhone 17 Pro's overall performance compared to its predecessor, as the iPhone can maintain lower temperatures during demanding tasks.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will feature a sleek titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. While it may also include a vapor chamber, only one source has reported this so far. Due to differences in materials, even with the same chip as the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone Ultra may perform slightly worse in direct sunlight or during intensive tasks.
